study_identification.title: Normative trajectories of R1, R2*, and magnetic susceptibility in basal ganglia on healthy ageing

study_characteristics.study_objective: To establish the normative trajectories of R1, R2*, and magnetic susceptibility in the basal ganglia at 3T throughout a normal lifespan, and to validate the utility of these trajectories in a clinical cohort with Parkinson's disease.

dataset_name.answer: Advanced Brain Imaging on Ageing and Memory (ABRIM)

imaging_modality.answer: T1-weighted MRI; T2*-weighted MRI; Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping (QSM)

quality_checking_detail.answer: Visual data curation was performed by three raters. 41 participants were excluded due to incidental findings and/or not fulfilling quality criteria (e.g., whole brain coverage, correct brain extraction, no visible motion artifacts).

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: The study used a single site for the primary analysis.

predictor_effects.answer: Sex and Hemisphere were corrected for based on GLM results before GPR. Age was the primary predictor in the GPR model.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The model accounts for age-related changes in variance (heteroscedasticity) and corrects for sex and hemisphere effects.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: The normative models we derived take into account the changes in variance across age, thereby enabling the derivation of z- statistics with new data...We utilised the GLM model to account for the inter- hemispherical difference in this work.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study used 10-fold cross-validation to evaluate the model on the training data.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: Gaussian Process Regression (GRP) ... was used to compute the normative trajectory of the sex- and hemispheric- corrected qMRI metrics as a function of age with 10-fold cross- validation.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study did not use a separate independent dataset from the same domain for validation.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The normative models were validated on an independent dataset (PPP) containing healthy controls and Parkinson's disease patients.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: Validation of the normative models derived from the ABRIM data was performed by applying the normative models to the PPP cohort.

clinical_groups_age.answer: PD: mean 60.9, sd 9.0; HC: mean 58.2, sd 9.2

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Two-sample t-tests were performed to compare the z-scores and the median qMRI values of each structure between the healthy controls and Parkinson's disease patients.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study established normative trajectories for qMRI parameters in the basal ganglia, showing age-dependent changes, and demonstrated their utility by identifying significant deviations in Parkinson's disease patients in the substantia nigra.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Normative models revealed quadratic R1 trajectories and linear R2*/χ trajectories in the basal ganglia. Validation in an independent cohort of Parkinson's disease patients showed significantly higher z-scores for R2* and χ in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) (p < 0.001) and pars reticulata (SNr) (p < 0.05) compared to healthy controls, confirming the model's ability to detect disease-related alterations.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study notes that derived models may not be universally valid across different studies due to variations in acquisition parameters and processing pipelines. The use of a single control cohort for the main analysis, although large, might have study-associated biases. The analysis of hemispheric differences was based on a correction rather than separate modeling.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study highlights the potential of using normative models of qMRI to detect subtle, spatially specific brain changes in neurological disorders, moving beyond traditional case-control comparisons.

general_notes.general_notes: The study provides a comprehensive analysis of qMRI parameters in the basal ganglia across the adult lifespan. The use of a large, well-characterized healthy cohort and validation in a clinical population strengthens the findings. The public availability of the data and processing scripts is a major contribution to the field.
